report.title: The buying committee in API management and secure connectivity, 2026-Q3

method.what_was_done: A WhyUser buying committee was simulated against each page in this set: every committee role, across behavioural states, under one strategy directive per page.
method.identifiers: Company ids in this report are per-edition pseudonyms. They are minted from a secret held by the publisher, they are not stable between editions, and they correspond to no internal or public identifier. An id here cannot be matched to an id anywhere else, including one you may hold for the same company.
method.counted_vs_simulated: Counted findings are page facts a stranger can confirm in ten seconds, and the failure modes computed arithmetically from them. Simulated findings come from the committee runs: role reads, handoffs, frictions and fixes. They are directional, reported as runs, and never presented as measured traffic.

Our page speaks to more than one member of the buying committee.
Our page says what we do, not only what category we are in.
A security reviewer can find at least one enterprise-readiness signal.
Our page names the team this is for and the kind of company they work at.
If the only path forward is a conversation, the page earns it with numbers first.
Where our page names what a buyer does today, it also names what is wrong with it.
Our page names an enemy and frames a pain someone is already paying for.
Our page shows proof of some kind: logos, a named quote, a certification, a case.
Our page names what a buyer does today instead of buying from us.
If we sell self-serve, a buyer can see real prices without talking to us.
Every number in our hero has proof sitting next to it.

assessment.note: Each check is the healthy side of a failure mode counted across this category. Bands come from how these companies actually scored, not from a rule of thumb. Scores are expressed out of ten however many checks a page could be assessed on, so editions stay comparable.

items.headline: it does not reach your funnel data
items.body: On 36 of 36, the decision stopped moving between two people inside the buying organisation. That reader had already been convinced by the page, so the failure leaves no bounce, no drop-off and no abandoned form. Nothing in an analytics tool is shaped like it.

items.headline: the repair is a page change, not a rebuild
items.body: Of 108 fixes written across this census, 77 are low effort. This is not a redesign, a repositioning or a quarter of work.

items.headline: and the category is not fixing it
items.body: The friction most often carried with no fix proposed against it is “claim made, never substantiated”, on 12 companies. A friction that shows up everywhere and attracts no fix is either invisible to the people writing these pages, or one the category has quietly decided it cannot solve.

items.headline: and traffic is being bought for these pages today

asks.placement: after the census plate, and again at the end
asks.title: Which row is yours
asks.body: Every company here is real and anonymised. If you market one of the 36 products in this census you have a row, a score on all ten checks, and a committee read we have not published.
asks.why: Curiosity peaks immediately after the reader has seen the grid and failed to find themselves. This is the highest-intent moment on the page and the only one that self-qualifies: nobody outside the category asks.

asks.title: If we read your page wrong
asks.body: Every finding here is anchored to a page fact you can go and check. If we got one wrong on your page, we will re-run it and publish the difference.
asks.why: Almost nobody takes it, and the offer is the credibility. It is also the only route by which a company can consent to being named.

asks.title: Which category next
asks.body: We run one of these per category. Tell us which one to measure next.
asks.why: Demand-validated roadmap, and a list of people who asked to be measured.

score_outcomes.next: Two of the checks you missed are the ones this category fails most. Start there, and ask for your row to see which reader each one cost.
This is the trap. The median page passes most of these and the committee still stalls, because the checks a page passes are not the checks that survive being handed to somebody else.
The page facts are in order, so the remaining risk is in the handoffs between readers, which no page checklist can see. Ask for your row.
